text.text: A ten-minute tour for everyone who packs, answers customers or orders stock. Read it once; the checklists at the end are the weekly rhythm.
: one row per thing you list, with price, landed cost (goods plus freight, per unit), margin, supplier and packed weight. Units on hand, units sold and sales add up from the rows below.
: one row per option you can actually pick off a shelf: a colour, a size, a scent. Each has its stock, reorder point, reorder quantity, what is already on order and its shelf.
: every order with channel, SKU, quantity, shipping charged against what the label cost, carrier, tracking and who is packing it.
: what you have ordered from suppliers and when it is due.
: every send-back and exchange, why, and where the item goes.
: who buys and who you buy from.

The carrier collects at 3. Anything not packed by 2 pm moves to the next morning's list; the packer tells support so they can answer if a customer asks.
Wholesale orders ship by courier or are picked up. Count twice, pack by case, and put the invoice in the first box. Ask the buyer to count on arrival and report shortages within 48 hours.

Twenty minutes every Monday keeps you from selling something you do not have, or running out of your best seller in December.
Numbers in a system drift: a broken mug nobody logged, a candle given to a friend, a miscount when stock came in. Counting the fast sellers every week and everything else once a month keeps
honest, which keeps the Reorder flag honest.
Count every SKU on the A and B shelves (mugs, bowls, candles: the fast sellers). Do the linens and packaging on the first Monday of the month.
If a count is more than two units off, write a line on the SKU page: what you found and the likely reason.
: on hand plus what is on order is above the reorder point.
: on hand plus on order has reached the reorder point. Put the reorder quantity on the next purchase order.
: zero on hand. Mark the option as sold out on every channel the same day.

A reorder point is what you sell during the supplier's lead time, plus a cushion. Example: the fig and tea 8 oz tin sells about 12 a week. Wick and Wax takes 10 days. Twelve a week is about 17 in 10 days; add 8 for a busy week and the reorder point is 25. Raise points in October for the holiday rush and lower them again in January.

A fair, fast return turns a disappointed customer into a repeat one. Decide quickly, explain clearly, refund on the day the item arrives.
Thirty days from delivery to ask for a return.

Damaged or wrong item: ask for one photo. For anything under 40 dollars, send the replacement and skip the return; the postage costs more than the item.

Treat an exchange as a new order at no charge, linked in the return's notes. Ship the new item as soon as the return is in transit, not when it arrives. Customers notice.
